key_insight: The paper derives exact closed-form post-acoustic solutions for the piston effect in near-critical fluids, showing how boundary heating drives a rapid bulk thermal response through a pressure-coupled diffusion process.
engineering_relevance: These results provide a compact analytical tool for predicting heat transfer and thermal transients in supercritical-fluid systems, with relevance to cryogenic, space, and high-pressure thermal management design.
method: Assume a post-acoustic approximation with spatially uniform, time-dependent bulk pressure.
Solve the linear diffusion problem exactly in 1D Cartesian and spherical geometries for first- and second-kind boundary conditions.
Include container heat capacity via an effective homogeneous boundary condition to compare against experiments.
evidence_signal: The analytical predictions are compared with Spacelab D-2 experimental data and reported to agree well without numerical simulation.
watch_item: The formulation relies on linearization and a post-acoustic assumption, so accuracy may degrade when acoustic effects, strong nonlinearity, or multidimensional geometry become important.
paper_title: Exact analytical solutions for the piston effect in supercritical fluids under post-acoustic approximation -- Short-time asymptotics, thermal penetration depth and comparison with the Spacelab D-2 experiments
